clue.text: Putting right soldiers in the middle

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a regiment of soldiers
medial means situated in the middle

explanation.surface: Troops are being deployed to the centre to sort something out.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedial work is corrective, done to fix a fault.

clue.text: An apology for a dance

explanation.surface: Someone says sorry in order to get a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a polite apologetic interruption, and also an old-time dance where partners may be cut in on.

clue.text: Withdraw arms after English agreed

indicators.note: after places the weapons word behind the English and agreed pieces

parts.note: at one means in agreement
swords are weapons, arms

explanation.surface: A disarmament deal is struck once the English consent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdraw' looks military beside 'arms', but it means retract a statement.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to retract something said, admitting one was wrong.

clue.text: Ancients devised this precedent

indicators.note: devised suggests the letters of the old-timers word are contrived into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The old ones set an example for later generations to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A precedent is an earlier case or example cited as a guide.

clue.text: Fish booby's caught, taking it easy

indicators.note: caught shows the fish holding the fool inside it

parts.note: ling is a fish of the cod family
a booby is a fool, an oaf; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A fool lazes about while fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Loafing is idling, lounging about with no effort.

clue.text: Can cough wreak havoc?

parts.note: may means can, as in giving permission
hem is a small clearing of the throat

explanation.surface: Could a fit of coughing cause chaos?
explanation.walkthrough: 'wreak' is a link word joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is chaos and disorder, a synonym.

clue.text: Service brought about love game

indicators.note: brought about means turned round, so the service letters are read backwards

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A tennis serve leads to a love game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' and 'love' suggest tennis; faro is an old gambling card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Faro is a card game for gambling, played against a banker.

clue.text: A tie? Exactly, a tie

parts.note: dead means exactly, as in dead centre
a tie is a round of a competition, and a heat is a qualifying round

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it was a tie and is told yes, exactly that.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'a tie' phrases carry different senses: a drawn result, and a round in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A race finishing level with no winner is a draw.

clue.text: False teeth are easily obtainable

parts.note: dentures are mounted on a dental plate, and the idiom for handed over with no effort uses the same word

explanation.surface: Dentures can be had without difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means given to someone without effort, served up ready.

clue.text: Style of singing primarily suited to a jazz fan

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of suited is used

parts.note: cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast

explanation.surface: A particular vocal style is said to suit a jazz lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Scat is improvised jazz vocalising using nonsense syllables.

clue.text: Draught beer is no longer in danger

explanation.surface: Beer on tap is described as safe now.
explanation.definitionFit: Draught beer is drawn from the cask, and the idiom means past peril, safe at last.

clue.text: Wrongly inserts 'Lewes' in place of 'Lewis'

indicators.note: wrongly suggests the letters of the two words are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A typist puts the Sussex town in place of the Hebridean island.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewes is a town in Sussex; Lewis is an island in the Outer Hebrides, off Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish island group, the Outer Hebrides, includes the isle of Lewis.

clue.text: Part bearing a flower

parts.note: to part is to separate, sever
N, north, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A section carries a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is read as something that flows, a river: the Severn is Britain's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosswords use flower for a river, a thing that flows.

clue.text: Someone unoriginally called me a sneak — it's not right

indicators.note: not right suggests the letters are wrongly placed and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Somebody with a borrowed name insults me, which is unfair.
explanation.definitionFit: A namesake bears the same name as another person, so the name is not original to them.

clue.text: Children dread being caught in tangle

indicators.note: the dread word is held within the children word

parts.note: seed means offspring, children
awe is fearful reverence, dread

explanation.surface: Children are afraid of getting caught up in a knot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tangle' looks like a knot but is a kind of kelp.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangle is a name for large brown kelp found on the shore.

clue.text: Scam necessitates duplicate card being hidden

indicators.note: the card is concealed inside the duplicate word

parts.note: same means identical, a duplicate
the king is a court card

explanation.surface: A con trick requires a copied card to be kept out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin game is a swindle or rigged gamble.

clue.text: Keeping up with Jack, run towards the sunrise

parts.note: jack is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
the sun rises in the east

explanation.surface: Someone keeps pace with Jack by running eastward.
explanation.definitionFit: Being level alongside, or up to date with, a matter.

clue.text: Scholar is clad in fine fabric, a fabulous creature

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate scholar

indicators.note: clad in means dressed in, so the fabric goes round the is

parts.note: silk is a fine fabric
taken as written

explanation.surface: An academic is dressed in silk, looking like a fantastic beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The basilisk is a legendary serpent whose glance could kill, a mythical beast.

clue.text: Seen in discos now — ballroom dancing

indicators.note: seen in means the letters are visible inside the following words

explanation.surface: Nowadays it appears in discos as ballroom dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' defines a party dance in which each couple splits to fetch new partners, so the dancers multiply.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowball is a party dance whose numbers grow as partners are drawn in.

clue.text: Lead a man to ignore the stars that are around and immovable

indicators.note: ignore means leave out, so the constellation letters are dropped from the run of words

parts.note: the answer runs forwards through these words, a hidden word in effect, and dropping the surrounding constellation letters is how the setter exposes it, so this is no coincidence
Leo is a constellation, a group of stars, and its letters sit around the remaining ones

explanation.surface: Persuade a fellow to disregard astrology and stand firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The constellation's letters are the first two and the last of the run 'Lead a man to', so they surround what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means unyielding, refusing to be moved.

clue.text: Find out about unusual sort of radiation

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged find surrounds the unusual word
out means put out of order, so the letters of find are rearranged

parts.note: rare means unusual

explanation.surface: Discover a strange kind of radiation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges FIND into INFD, split to go 'about' RARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Infrared is electromagnetic radiation beyond the red end of the visible spectrum.

clue.text: Predatory bird, a sort of parrot

indicators.note: sort of suggests a rough version, a reordering of the bird's letters

explanation.surface: A bird of prey is described as a kind of parrot.
explanation.definitionFit: A raptor is a bird of prey such as a hawk or eagle.

clue.text: High-ranking Spanish gentleman to whom I was introduced

indicators.note: the letter I is put into the Spanish word

parts.note: señor is Spanish for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A distinguished Spaniard to whom the speaker was presented.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior means higher in rank or standing.

clue.text: Ponce the French clapped into irons, a reaction to horror

indicators.note: clapped into irons means imprisoned, so the pieces go inside the irons word

parts.note: a goose is a tailor's smoothing iron
a ponce is British slang for a pimp
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A procurer and his French associate are shackled, prompting shudders.
explanation.walkthrough: A tailor's goose is a heavy pressing iron, plural gooses.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumps rising on the skin are a response to fear or cold.

clue.text: Formerly, 1/100

parts.note: 1 is spelt out and the Roman numeral for 100, C, divides it

explanation.walkthrough: Write 1 as a word and the Roman numeral for 100 as C, then split the word with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at one time in the past, formerly.

clue.text: For the Speaker, single accommodation

indicators.note: for the speaker means as heard, so the word for single is said aloud

parts.note: lone means single, solitary

explanation.surface: A single room for the Speaker of the Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodation' means a financial arrangement, money lent.
explanation.definitionFit: An accommodation is a sum lent, an advance of credit.

clue.text: A bus to mooch around? That takes the biscuit

indicators.note: around shows the idle-wandering word placed round the other pieces

parts.note: to moon about is to mooch, wander idly
bus is old slang for a motor car

explanation.surface: Wandering about on a bus, someone finds it beyond belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes the biscuit' sounds like the idiom for outrageous, but the biscuit is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaroon is an almond or coconut biscuit.

clue.text: Receipts set to rise at the bar

parts.note: takes are money received, takings
ilk means a set, kind or class

explanation.surface: Income is expected to go up in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the bar' is the legal profession, not a pub; to take silk is to become a Queen's (now King's) Counsel.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming a senior barrister is a promotion within the legal profession.
